b2-11-01.title: Communicative Challenge: After the Dream
b2-11-01.scenario: Captain Störr has come home through the foggy streets and Lizzy asks what is wrong. You are Captain Störr and answer.
b2-11-01.prompt: Tell Lizzy what happened to you and how you feel now.
cues: Say that a strange dream upset you
Say that you calmed down after the talk
b2-11-01.target: Egy különös álom felzaklatott, de a beszélgetésünk után megnyugodtam.
b2-11-01.english: A strange dream upset me, but after our talk I calmed down.
b2-11-01.canDo: I can distinguish transitive psychological verbs (-ít / -tat) from their middle/intransitive counterparts (-ul/-ül, -ódik/-ődik, -szik)

b2-11-02.title: Communicative Challenge: Brooding in the Fog
b2-11-02.scenario: Lizzy asks Captain Störr why he walked about so long in the fog. You are Captain Störr and answer.
b2-11-02.prompt: Tell Lizzy what you did while you walked.
cues: Say that you brooded over her words
Say that you doubted your own thoughts
b2-11-02.target: A szavaidon tépelődtem, és kételkedtem a saját gondolataimban.
b2-11-02.english: I brooded over your words, and I doubted my own thoughts.
b2-11-02.canDo: I can form and interpret behavioral and self-directed verbs ending in -kodik/-kedik/-ködik

b2-11-03.title: Communicative Challenge: Facing My Suspicion
b2-11-03.scenario: Lizzy asks Captain Störr what he understood on his walk. You are Captain Störr and answer.
b2-11-03.prompt: Tell Lizzy what you faced and what you did with your own insecurity.
cues: Say that you faced your suspicion
Say that you projected your insecurity onto her
b2-11-03.target: Szembenéztem a gyanakvásommal, mert a saját bizonytalanságomat vetítettem ki rád.
b2-11-03.english: I faced my suspicion, because I projected my own insecurity onto you.
b2-11-03.canDo: I can use B2 psychological verbs with their mandatory case frames (szembenéz + -val/-vel, belemerül + -ba/-be, kivetít + -ra/-re)

b2-11-04.title: Communicative Challenge: Do Not Torment Yourself
b2-11-04.scenario: Captain Störr sits silent in the room and withdraws into himself. You are Lizzy and speak to him.
b2-11-04.prompt: Tell the captain not to withdraw into himself and not to torment himself.
cues: Tell him not to withdraw into himself
Tell him not to torment himself with suspicion
b2-11-04.target: Ne zárkózz magadba, és ne kínozd magad gyanakvással!
b2-11-04.english: Do not withdraw into yourself, and do not torment yourself with suspicion!
b2-11-04.canDo: I can use inflected forms of the reflexive pronoun maga/önmaga across psychological idioms

b2-11-05.title: Communicative Challenge: Peace at Last
b2-11-05.scenario: Late in the evening Lizzy asks Captain Störr how he feels after the talk. You are Captain Störr and answer.
b2-11-05.prompt: Tell Lizzy what you faced and how you feel now.
cues: Say that you faced your jealousy
Say that you made peace with yourself
Say that the tension dissolved in you
b2-11-05.target: Szembenéztem a féltékenységemmel, és végre megbékéltem önmagammal. A feszültség feloldódott bennem.
b2-11-05.english: I faced my jealousy, and I have finally made peace with myself. The tension has dissolved in me.
b2-11-05.canDo: I can synthesize valency alternations, -kodik/-ódik verbs, and reflexive pronouns in a psychological character study

b2-11-consolidation.title: Communicative Challenge: What I Understand Now
b2-11-consolidation.scenario: Lizzy asks Captain Störr what he wants to change. You are Captain Störr and answer.
b2-11-consolidation.prompt: Tell Lizzy why you will not withdraw into yourself any more.
cues: Say that anxiety does not dissolve by itself
Say that you will not withdraw into yourself
Say that you will tell her your dream
b2-11-consolidation.target: A szorongás nem oldódik meg magától, ezért nem zárkózom többé magamba, hanem elmondom neked az álmomat.
b2-11-consolidation.english: Anxiety does not dissolve by itself, so I will not withdraw into myself any more, but tell you my dream.
b2-11-consolidation.canDo: I can accurately contrast transitive (-ít/-tat) and middle/intransitive (-ul/-ül/-ódik/-szik) psychological verbs
